    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • Sources indicate that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases confirmed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," remarked Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    Sources indicate that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases confirmed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," remarked Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    Bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    Recent findings suggest that the Treasury Department stated last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

    Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "big toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Sources indicate that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah noted. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    Recent findings suggest that the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah remarked. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    According to recent reports, "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh mentioned in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1474 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1474 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hilton is making a massive play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hilton is making a massive play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    Recent findings suggest that you can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    Industry observers note that for breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    Industry observers note that for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    It has been revealed that you can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    According to recent reports, one of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    In a recent development, next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    One of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    It has been revealed that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rlx Technology ›.

    In a recent development, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 20, 2026, RLX (RLX -4.11%) reported net revenue of RMB 1.92 billion, a 70% year-over-year increase driven by international expansion. The organization is shifting from a domestic manufacturer into a global distributor with direct access to thousands of European stores. That shift expands its reach, but it also alters its gross margin profile and changes how it allocates capital. Three things management remarked stand out.

    Acquiring a Western European distribution platform added direct access to tens of thousands of storefronts and a business-to-business (B2B) network of independent merchants. That direct connection gives RLX immediate feedback on store inventory turnover, helping it tailor products faster than remote competitors can.

    It has been revealed that integrating lower-margin distribution platforms compresses headline gross margins, but management generates cash to fund both acquisition opportunities and capital returns. It tanked in the first few months of the year on concerns about slowing cloud growth and massive artificial intelligence (AI) spending. But since then, cloud growth has accelerated, and investors are recognizing that AI spending has been necessary to add the capacity needed to grow cloud businesses.

    This was evident in Amazon's performance in the third quarter. Net sales rose 12% to $202 billion while operating income surged 61% year over year to $28.1 billion. That jump in operating income was driven by its higher-margin Amazon Web Services (AWS), its cloud business, which saw operating income increase 56% to $17.8 billion. Net sales with AWS jumped 39% to $46 billion, its fastest growth rate in nearly five years.

    Industry observers note that it also reported a backlog of $578 billion, up triple digits year over year. The recent tech stock slide has kept Amazon at a historically low valuation, making it a great time to capitalize.

    Sources indicate that there are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel aims than the groupings suggest.

    Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

    » Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

    Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

    Sources indicate that they’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

    According to recent reports, you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel aims before choosing.

    Each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

    According to recent reports, through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

    Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

    Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

    Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

    Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

    Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

    Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

    Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

    Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

    Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

    Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

    Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

    The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

    According to recent reports, new lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

    Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

    Recent findings suggest that global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

    Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

    Earn 1 status point for every 25 points transferred to Atmos Rewards from Bilt or Marriott Bonvoy.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Sources indicate that through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

    If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

    In a recent development, if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you’ll earn 3 Atmos points per $1 spent on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines purchases, dining and foreign transactions. The last bonus category can be especially useful for frequent international travelers.

    It has been revealed that this community has a similar setup to Global Locals, but most of its bonus destinations are in the U.S. Here’s what you can get:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    According to recent reports, through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    In a recent development, this community would be an excellent choice if your upcoming travels include several of these airports, even if dining isn't the main reason for your trips. If dining out is one of your favorite activities, check out the best credit cards for restaurants.

    It has been revealed that active Escapes focuses on airports in outdoor-oriented destinations that are all in the U.S., save one. Benefits here are:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    Recent findings suggest that while these airports are gateways to national parks and other natural attractions, you don’t have to be an outdoor enthusiast to benefit. Like before, don’t let the heading sway you. Rather, consider the destinations before you decide.

    Families On the Go might appeal to you if you redeem Atmos Rewards for your children. Benefits include:.

    Get 20% of your points back on eligible award flights for kids 12 and under after you complete your trip.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, these destinations qualify for bonus points and status points:.

    Industry observers note that this community may be especially valuable if you regularly book award flights for children 12 and under. Even if you don't travel with kids, it could be worth considering if its qualifying airports align better with your travel aims than those of other communities.

    Exclusively for Alaska residents, Club 49 offers rewards that are focused on travel to, from and within the state:.

    Two free checked bags when traveling to or from Alaska on Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines.

    Three free checked bags when traveling within Alaska on Alaska Airlines.

    Two Travel Now discounts per year for 30% off one-way refundable Y-class fares on Alaska Airlines, booked within four days of departure for travel to, from or within Alaska.

    Ship cargo within Alaska for $49 plus tax (weight, size and content limits apply).

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Baggage benefits don’t combine with other free checked bag allowances, such as those that come with some Alaska credit cards. However, they apply to everyone traveling on the same reservation.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus offers:.

    While this community is only for Alaskans, you might decide one of the other communities more closely matches your travel prepares — especially if you already have an Alaska credit card with free baggage benefits. However, if you ship a lot of cargo or think you’ll use the Travel Now discounts, those are special benefits that may sway you to choose Club 49.

    Hawaii residents have their own community just for them: Huaka’i by Hawaiian. It offers benefits focused on interisland travel:.

    Two free checked bags on neighbor island flights on Hawaiian Airlines, including sports equipment like surfboards and golf bags.

    Quarterly fare discounts of 10% off one neighbor island booking, or 20% off for eligible Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard® and Atmos™ Rewards Visa® cardholders.

    According to recent reports, earn 50% more points and status points on flights between Hawaiian islands beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Sources indicate that seven destinations are in Hawaii, with one on the mainland and two international cities. If you live in Hawaii and like to hop between islands, this community is a strong choice.

    Don’t be persuaded by the names of the communities. Look a little deeper, because there’s a lot of overlap between destination lists. Compare the options against your upcoming travel plans.

    You can change communities once per calendar year, so you aren’t locked in to your initial choice indefinitely. However, switching communities resets your destination-challenge progress, but you’ll retain any points you’ve already earned.

    If your home airport (or one you visit frequently) is already on a community’s list, you may have an easier time earning points. Also consider whether a particular community benefit, such as free checked bags or points back on award flights for kids, outweighs the destination challenge.

    Finally, pay attention to airport codes. For example, Tokyo’s Narita (NRT) and Haneda (HND) appear on different community lists. Fresh York’s qualifying airport is JFK, while it is DCA in Washington, D.C. If you have a choice between airports, check which one qualifies for your community’s challenge.

    Should You Invest $1,000 in Bloom Energy Right Now?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (724 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Earlier this year, things seemed to be going exactly right for fuel-cell manufacturer Bloom Energy (BE -15.30%).
    • In a recent development, it's not hard to see why.
    • In that context, new orders for Bloom's fuel-cell systems were coming in hot: First Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) contracted for 1.2 gigawatts (GW) of capacity, then Brookfield Asset Management (BAM -2.53%) expanded its financing framework with Bloom for AI projects from $5 billion to a whopping $25 billion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Steven Porrello – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

    Earlier this year, things seemed to be going exactly right for fuel-cell manufacturer Bloom Energy (BE -15.30%).

    In a recent development, it's not hard to see why. The race to build AI data centers had stimulated such an enormous appetite for electricity that developers, facing grid bottlenecks and tight construction timelines, simply couldn't afford to wait years for traditional power grid connections.

    In that context, new orders for Bloom's fuel-cell systems were coming in hot: First Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) contracted for 1.2 gigawatts (GW) of capacity, then Brookfield Asset Management (BAM -2.53%) expanded its financing framework with Bloom for AI projects from $5 billion to a whopping $25 billion.

    Both were significant developments for Bloom's business, and Wall Street absolutely agreed: The stock soared to an all-time high of roughly $350, more than quadrupling in value from where it started the year.

    If you take a look at Bloom's stock chart today, however, you'll see a different picture: It has fallen from its high to roughly $168 per share.

    That raises the obvious question: What the heck is happening? And, more importantly, should you take this as an occasion to buy Bloom stock?

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that for starters, Bloom is a fuel cell manufacturer. In simple terms, it makes equipment that let data centers and other customers generate electricity on-site rather than waiting years to connect to the grid. These fuel cells are also a source of (relatively) clean power: Instead of burning fuel, they use an electrochemical reaction to convert fuel (such as natural gas) into electricity. It's a pretty neat concept, and it is especially useful for those who need round-the-clock power.

    As mentioned, Bloom stock soared earlier this year as sales of Bloom boxes went through the roof. This hasn't changed. Indeed, third-quarter sales surged 138% year over year to $1.24 billion, prompting management (yet again!) to raise full-year revenue guidance to between $4.4 billion and $4.6 billion. For perspective, its full-year 2025 revenue was about $2 billion.

    What has changed, however, is the environment, or more specifically: Wall Street's willingness to pay sky-high valuations for companies associated with the AI boom. Investors have become increasingly concerned about the billions being poured into AI infrastructure, and Bloom, whose future growth is tied to AI spending, has found itself caught in this broader wave of bearish sentiment.

    The irony, of course, is that the very numbers that once sent Bloom's stock soaring are no longer enough to reassure investors. But why is that?

    If I could capture that shift in perspective in an image, it would be this: Bloom's breathtaking growth this year is like a star's light. It's brilliant to look at, but it tells us more about the past than it does the future. It tells us just how bullish data center developers were on AI infrastructure earlier this year, but it doesn't necessarily indicate how Bloom will fare if that spending slows or stalls.

    In other words, Bloom's extraordinary financial results could be a lagging indicator of an AI spending frenzy that is fading, while its stock price reflects anxiety about what will come next.

    So, given that Wall Street is concerned about Bloom's future sales, should you reverse course and buy?

    Recent findings suggest that personally, I think this is a great opportunity to pick up Bloom stock. The reaction to concerns over data center construction strikes me as a bit overdone. Even if AI spending slows, the underlying problem Bloom is solving -- an electricity grid struggling to keep up with rising demands -- isn't going away anytime soon. The stock might be volatile today, but for those willing to hold through the volatility, I think today's sell-off offers an attractive opportunity to buy a company with long-term growth potential.

    By Katie Brockman – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    It's been a lucrative year for the stock market, with the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) notching more than two dozen record highs in 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that however, the headwinds have been coming in strong lately. Volatility within the tech sector has rattled Wall Street, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) fell into correction territory after plunging nearly 12% from its recent peak, as of this writing.

    Sources indicate that the bad news for investors is that no bull market can last forever, and it's only a matter of time before we face a pullback. However, Warren Buffett has some timeless advice about how to prepare your portfolio for a potential market crash or recession.

    Warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

    In late 1999, just four months before the dot-com bubble officially popped, Warren Buffett issued a warning to investors in an essay for Fortune. He emphasized that while new advancements in technology could transform society, that doesn't necessarily make them smart investments.

    Using airlines as an example, Buffett noted that although air travel was revolutionary, 129 airlines had gone bankrupt over the previous 20 years. Televisions and radios fell into the same category as "glamorous businesses that dramatically changed our lives but concurrently failed to deliver rewards to U.S. investors.".

    Sources indicate that the dot-com bubble eventually proved Buffett's point. While the internet went on to fundamentally transform the world, countless tech stocks crashed and burned in the early 2000s.

    "The key to investing is not assessing how much an industry is going to affect society, or how much it will grow," Buffett explained, "but rather determining the competitive advantage of any given company and, above all, the durability of that advantage.".

    Industry observers note that while it's impossible to say how the market will fare in the coming months, the dot-com bubble serves as a valuable lesson. Artificial intelligence (AI) as a technology could be revolutionary, but that doesn't mean every AI stock will be a good investment. Inevitably, some stocks will flounder during the next downturn.

    In a recent development, the best move investors can make now is to load up on a wide variety of quality stocks with robust business fundamentals. While all stocks are vulnerable to short-term volatility, those with strong competitive advantages are the most likely to recover and deliver long-term growth.

    Healthy companies will likely thrive over time. Although the S&P 500 lost almost half of its value between 2000 and 2002, the index soared by more than 200% in the two decades following the dot-com bubble.

    If we're headed toward a similar bear market, not all stocks will recover. But healthy companies will fuel decades of growth, and the investors who look past the hype and focus on quality stocks will reap the biggest rewards.

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Industry observers note that A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to newly introduced inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    If PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you blueprint to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    By Katie Brockman – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:41PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) made history this week with the largest stock market debut on record, securing $81 billion in funding and surpassing SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO) earlier this year.

    There was no shortage of investor enthusiasm either, as the stock popped by more than 17% during its first day of trading. While nobody can say how the stock will fare in the coming days or weeks, I predict that some Anthropic investors are about to learn a hard, expensive lesson.

    In a recent development, dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

    Blockbuster IPOs are often turbulent straight out of the gate, experiencing extreme price swings in their initial weeks and months.

    It has been revealed that spaceX, for example, has fallen by more than 20% from its initial price, as of this writing. Semiconductor breakout star SK Hynix has plunged by nearly 30% since it debuted in July, and Meta Platforms – then known as Facebook – sank by more than 50% in its first three months of trading in 2012.

    In Meta's case, the stock eventually bounced back, delivering total returns of around 1,400% since its IPO. But the investors who reaped those rewards were those who stayed invested through all the ups and downs rather than expecting immediate riches.

    According to recent reports, the same thing could be mentioned for Anthropic. Over time, it could be a lucrative investment. The manufacturer recently generated $17 billion in third-quarter revenue, significantly outpacing its $1.4 billion figure from 2025.

    But Anthropic also has some major bills to keep up with. Its IPO prospectus disclosed over $900 billion in expense commitments and a $104 billion net operating loss in 2026, and time will tell whether the company's revenue is sufficient to fund the enormous computing power its technology demands.

    Sources indicate that this isn't to say that Anthropic is a bad investment. But as with any IPO, there are a lot of unknowns right now, and anything could happen in the coming weeks and months.

    If you believe in the business model and are willing to hold your investment for at least a few years despite any potential short-term volatility, it could be a smart buy – assuming it's part of a well-diversified portfolio.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    However, investors who are buying primarily because of the hype around the stock, hoping to make a quick buck, have the most to lose. The short term is likely to be a bumpy ride, and those who are only buying with the hope of earning a fortune overnight could end up sorely disappointed.

    Fundamentals beat hype every time, and the strongest investments are those with solid underlying business fundamentals and long-term growth potential.

    Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure organization Oracle (ORCL) recently revealed better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," stated Gesuale.

    Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028.     • In a recent development, one of the biggest investment opportunities in the market right now is in memory chip stocks, with Micron (MU -13.89%) and Sandisk (SNDK -16.05%) being the two best options.
    • It has been revealed that there are many unknowns surrounding Nvidia right now.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:03PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›.

    Nvidia has grabbed all the headlines in recent weeks, mainly over what's going on with former CEO Jensen Huang. This has pummeled the stock, but there are other stocks benefiting from the same tailwinds as Nvidia that don't have the same headline risk right now.

    In a recent development, one of the biggest investment opportunities in the market right now is in memory chip stocks, with Micron (MU -13.89%) and Sandisk (SNDK -16.05%) being the two best options. But are they better than Nvidia? Let's take a look.

    It has been revealed that there are many unknowns surrounding Nvidia right now. Whether it's questions about how much of its chip sales may be going to China through third parties, or whether all of the demand was legitimate, nobody knows. However, one point that's not up for debate is that demand for AI computing is real, and it has stretched memory chip suppliers to their limits.

    Both Micron and Sandisk have sold out of production capacity, and it could be that way for many years, despite both companies opening newly introduced facilities in the near future to raise capacity. Micron's management team told investors that it expects memory chip market conditions to be worse in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, an incredible statement, given how bad things are right now. This will keep memory chip prices elevated for some time, which is fantastic news for investors.

    Both have a long history of being highly cyclical companies, with good times when demand is high and downturns when there is excess supply. Historically, these cycles don't last for much more than a year, and that's exactly what the market is expecting this time around.

    However, with AI hyperscalers needing much more computing capacity, this build-out could last until 2030 or beyond.

    That's a lot of time for both Sandisk and Micron to produce a ton of profits and reshape their futures, while also delivering huge investor returns on the way.

    Sources indicate that they are doing this by reshaping their business models. Sandisk and Micron are starting to sign long-term agreements with their clients, which sets a floor and a ceiling on memory prices. While this cuts out some of the peaks, it prevents these two from going into deep downturns when demand isn't as high. That sets their businesses up for long-term success.

    But can their returns trump Nvidia?

    Because the market is expecting a cyclical downturn any day now, each of these stocks is valued at a dirt cheap level.

    MU PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

    In a recent development, with both stocks at about 4 times this year's projected earnings (both companies are already in fiscal year 2027), that's a huge discount to the broader market. Nvidia is also cheap at about 10 times next year's earnings, but that pales in comparison to these two.

    Recent findings suggest that this makes these two excellent options, but only if the market comes around to valuing them properly. If the market keeps these two at low valuations due to concerns about their cyclical nature, these stocks may be duds. However, I don't see that happening.

    Both Sandisk and Micron have been repurchasing shares with their profits, which allows them to artificially boost earnings per share by decreasing the number of shares outstanding. This is nothing new and has been done successfully by many companies in the market.

    With their share prices low relative to their profits, each dollar spent on buybacks is more effective. This could deliver strong long-term returns and lead to outperformance of Nvidia.

    According to recent reports, although I think Nvidia will be OK over the long term, these two memory chip stocks may be a safer bet. Investors may want to see who the next CEO of Nvidia is before jumping back into the stock, and these two make for great alternatives with huge upside.

    • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's crucial to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • In a recent development, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's crucial to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    In a recent development, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Sources indicate that some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    According to recent reports, merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    In a recent development, merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    In a recent development, some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that indicates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Sources indicate that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    Sources indicate that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    It has been revealed that even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Industry observers note that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    In a recent development, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    In a recent development, which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    Industry observers note that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    It has been revealed that the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    Industry observers note that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    According to recent reports, apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a massive impact when you add several of them together.

    Industry observers note that understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    It has been revealed that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every time it looks like the S&P 500 is starting to drop, investors send it back up.
    • According to recent reports, however, there's bound to be a crash at some point, whether before the year's out or into the future.
    • Shopify is a top e-commerce company that provides services to e-commerce retailers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:33PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Shopify ›.

    Every time it looks like the S&P 500 is starting to drop, investors send it back up. As of this writing, it's no longer a double-digit increase year to date, but it's still up an admirable 7%. That's cautious optimism considering high inflation and rising interest rates.

    According to recent reports, however, there's bound to be a crash at some point, whether before the year's out or into the future. Whenever it happens, I would buy Shopify (SHOP -6.25%), Costco Wholesale (COST +0.76%), and e.l.f. Beauty (ELF -5.01%) stocks, all of which are great businesses but have rich price tags.

    Shopify is a top e-commerce company that provides services to e-commerce retailers. Its products range from total, all-inclusive websites to single products like payment systems or cross-border e-commerce, and it has moved from helping small businesses thrive to working with enterprise retailers like Estee Lauder's (EL -2.27%) Clinique and Lululemon Athletica (LULU -2.76%). That's because it takes away the pain points of companies having to develop these kinds of systems themselves, and it has developed a reputation for its services that make it their partner of choice.

    It has been revealed that even though it started as an e-commerce company, offering an easy path for small retailers to get online, it now calls itself simply a commerce company. It works with omnichannel retailers, unifying all of a company's brick-and-mortar and digital channels into one management system. The company describes its evolution as "However commerce evolves, Shopify will be the engine behind it. The merchants who are the backbone of the economy demand it of us.".

    In a recent development, despite inflation and lots of competition, Shopify's revenue is accelerating, up 32% year over year in the third quarter, and its gross merchandise volume (GMV), or the volume of sales on its platform from its clients, increased 29%. At $119 billion, it was higher than Amazon's (AMZN -4.10%) online and third-party sales of $116 billion. Amazon and Shopify have a partnership, too, whereby shoppers can use Amazon's Buy With Prime as a checkout through participating Shopify retailers.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that what's been stopping me from buying so far is the expensive price tag. At the current price, Shopify stock trades at 75 times trailing 12-month earnings, making it the most expensive stock on this list. That speaks to investor confidence, but it also builds in a lot of growth.

    Recent findings suggest that costco has a unique retail model that has proven to work through any kind of economic backdrop. It offers rock-bottom prices, but shoppers have to pay an annual fee to shop there. Considering its high renewal rates, consistently increasing membership metrics, and the number of members who upgrade to the executive membership, which costs double the standard rate, shoppers find the deal worthwhile.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, in fact, as inflation rises and customers become more cautious about spending, Costco’s sales growth has accelerated. In the 2026 fiscal fourth quarter (ended Aug. 30), sales increased 11.2% year over year, driven by a 9.4% increase in comparable sales. Some of that came from the company's gas stations as oil prices increased, and that's become an important growth driver. It's also highly profitable, and earnings per share (EPS) increased from $5.87 to $6.75.

    But it gets better. Costco also reports monthly metrics, and sales increased 13% in both September and October. On top of that, Costco just announced a $30 special dividend. Costco's regular dividend only yields 0.53%, but it pays a special dividend on average every two and a half years. Adding $30 to this year's payout would bring the effective yield to 3.2%.

    Recent findings suggest that however, Costco stock trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 53, which is a major premium to other retailers. The market obviously thinks it's worth it, but the stock is priced for perfection.

    Recent findings suggest that E.l.f. has carved out a niche in mass cosmetics as an eco-friendly brand with luxury dupes. It has become one of the largest companies of its kind, breaking into an industry dominated by legacy brands from which it’s pulling market share. It's also a newcomer in the luxury cosmetics industry, with its recent acquisition of Hailey Bieber's Rhode brand.

    In the 2027 fiscal Q2 (ended Sept. 30), sales increased 51% year over year, and gross margin increased 1.7 percentage points to 71%. E.l.f. stock has plunged after tariffs were introduced last year, but tariff refunds have improved its gross margin, and the stock has nearly doubled since it bottomed out last June.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It's the most popular cosmetics tech giant in the Piper Sandler (PIPR -4.03%) Taking Stock With Teens Survey, and Rhode is the third. It's now also the top or second-largest brand in 22 cosmetics categories, up from 11 in 2021.

    E.l.f. stock trades at 72 times trailing 12-month earnings, and if a broader market sell-off knocks that multiple closer to 40 or 45, I'd be ready to buy the stock—alongside Shopify and Costco.

    #96686. Intel Says It Just Signed Its First Customer for Its Most Advanced Chipmaking Process. The Stock Is Still More Than 60% Below Its June Record.

    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Intel Says It Just Signed Its First Customer for Its Most Advanced Chipmaking Process. The Stock Is Still More Than 60% Below Its June Record.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Intel (INTC -7.97%) CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated on Wednesday, Nov.
    • It has been revealed that he didn't name the customer.
    • It has been revealed that for a company still working to build a manufacturing business for other chip designers, the signing is a milestone.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:47PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Intel ›.

    "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Intel (INTC -7.97%) CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas.

    It has been revealed that he didn't name the customer. Intel's tech chief, Pushkar Ranade, later clarified on X that it had signed up for 18A-P, an upgraded version of 18A, the firm's most advanced manufacturing process. CNBC, which reported Tan's remarks, called it the first outside customer for Intel's 18A chips.

    It has been revealed that for a company still working to build a manufacturing business for other chip designers, the signing is a milestone. Shares haven't gotten a lift from it, though. Intel stock closed at around $55 on Tuesday, Nov. 17, and closed near $51 on Friday, Nov. 20 -- more than 60% below its record close of $140.94 on June 22.

    It has been revealed that I think that response makes sense. A signed customer starts a foundry relationship, but it isn't revenue yet. And Intel's own numbers show how small its outside manufacturing business still is.

    Intel might never tell investors who the customer is.

    "As is standard practice in the foundry business, I have consistently maintained that we will not disclose customer details," Tan said in prepared remarks for Intel's Oct. 29 earnings call.

    A name could still come from the customer's side. That same Wednesday, Intel noted Microsoft is the first company to announce use of its EMIB chip packaging tech, for chips Microsoft designs for its Azure cloud.

    Sure, outside companies have lined up behind Intel's latest technology before. Microsoft said in February 2024 that it planned to produce a chip design on Intel 18A. That September, Intel said it would build an artificial intelligence (AI) networking chip for Amazon's Amazon Web Services on 18A too. And in August, Japanese chip designer Socionext (OTC:SOCNF) said it would use 18A-P to develop custom chips.

    Still, Tan described this customer as signed, and Ranade linked it to 18A-P, so it's arguably the first customer signed for that process. Investors still don't know how many chips the customer prepares to buy and when Intel gets paid.

    In a recent development, intel's third-quarter foundry revenue grew 58% year over year to $6.7 billion, but most of it came from Intel's own product groups. Revenue from outside customers was $411 million, compared to $293 million in the second quarter and just $32 million a year before. Intel remarked the third-quarter jump came mostly from a non-recurring customer program. And in its quarterly filing, the tech giant said substantially all of its foundry business still supports manufacturing for Intel's own products.

    So, outside revenue is growing, but it's still around 6% of Intel's foundry sales, and the latest quarter relied on a one-time contract.

    According to recent reports, the losses are shrinking, at least. The foundry's third-quarter operating loss was $1.9 billion, around $240 million less than in the second quarter and almost $470 million less than a year before.

    Sources indicate that "These results represent meaningful progress, although we still have considerable work ahead of us to deliver a sustainably profitable Foundry business," CFO David Zinsner said in Intel's prepared remarks for the Oct. 29 call.

    Recent findings suggest that for the signing to matter to shareholders, I think the customer would have to come forward, since Intel won't name it. Intel's 18A-P process also has to move from risk production, which began in June, to volume.

    Intel says the process is on track to launch across its own products by year-end, but it hasn't mentioned when an outside customer's chips will follow. The deal also needs to show up as recurring outside revenue instead of another one-time program.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, more is at stake, too. Intel remarked in its last quarterly filing that committed demand for 14A, its next process, will dictate how fast and how far it expands manufacturing. That includes demand from potential significant outside customers. A signed 18A-P customer could help Intel get those commitments. But a deal on 18A-P isn't a commitment to 14A.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, investors are already paying plenty for Intel's future profits. At around $51, the stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 29 on next year's expected earnings. And Intel expects non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share to fall to $0.25 in the fourth quarter from $0.52 in the third.

    Tan's announcement is progress for a foundry that's mainly made Intel's own chips. But until the customer is named and its chips show up in Intel's outside revenue, I don't think it changes much for the stock.

    Sources indicate that leading scale, lowest gas prices, and heavy daily traffic: Home to over 1,800 locations across the Southeast and Midwest portions of the U.S., Murphy is the fourth-largest convenience-store chain in the country.     Thanks to a now-defunct partnership with Walmart (WMT +1.51%), most of Murphy's locations are next to some of the mega-retailer's stores, drawing heavy daily shopping traffic from customers typically focused on finding the best deals.

While the dividend currently yields only 0.54%, it pairs well with the company's buybacks, as the company can increase payments if the stock ever trades at a higher valuation.

    ULA Vulcan Launch Ends in Disaster for Amazon's Satellite Internet Ambitions

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that for months, Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) CEO Elon Musk had been making noises about ending commercial launches of its Falcon 9 rocket -- the rocket that, in 2025, rolled out more than 80% of all payloads to orbit worldwide.
    • Nine months ago, United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered an anomaly with one of its Vulcan Centaur rockets, forcing it to pause operations while it worked out a fix.
    • In a recent development, A successful launch would advance Amazon's effort to build a satellite communications system to rival SpaceX's Starlink.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Rich Smith – Nov 21, 2026 at 9:27PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Amazon ›.

    A crisis was forming in the space industry.

    Industry observers note that for months, Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) CEO Elon Musk had been making noises about ending commercial launches of its Falcon 9 rocket -- the rocket that, in 2025, rolled out more than 80% of all payloads to orbit worldwide. At the time, rockets from rival companies Arianespace, Blue Origin, and United Launch Alliance were all grounded for a variety of technical glitches.

    Nine months ago, United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered an anomaly with one of its Vulcan Centaur rockets, forcing it to pause operations while it worked out a fix. But at long last, ULA was ready to return to flight. In a mission slated for Nov. 15, Vulcan would return to flight, carrying a payload of 40 Leo communications satellites into orbit for customer Amazon (AMZN -4.10%).

    In a recent development, A successful launch would advance Amazon's effort to build a satellite communications system to rival SpaceX's Starlink. At the same time, it would alleviate the concerns of space companies worried that Falcon 9's retirement would deprive them of access to space. With ULA back in the race, there'd once again be an alternative to SpaceX.

    That's what a successful launch would have meant -- but it's not what actually happened.

    In a recent development, instead, for the first time in its history as a space manufacturer, ULA suffered a total mission failure -- all cargo lost. As ULA explained, its Vulcan rocket "lost telemetry and the mission at approximately 10 minutes into flight," although the real problem occurred before that.

    Vulcan Centaur includes two stages: BE-4 engines from Blue Origin power the Vulcan first stage, supplemented by RL10 side boosters from L3Harris(LHX -2.59%). In flight, the RL10s are first to drop off the rocket, followed by the entire first stage detaching approximately six minutes into flight. Then the Centaur second stage takes over and lifts the payload the rest of the way into orbit.

    In a recent development, after several days of examining the data, ULA now believes the RL10 boosters and the second-stage Centaur both performed nominally. The problem must therefore lie with the Vulcan first stage -- specifically, preliminary indications as of Wednesday suggest Vulcan's fuel supply to the BE-4 engines, rather than the engines themselves, was the culprit. This first stage performed poorly in the boost stage, failing to accelerate the vehicle sufficiently for the Centaur to lift the payload all the way into orbit.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    For Amazon, either culprit would be bad news.

    Aiming to accelerate its deployment of Leo satellites so that it can begin competing with SpaceX in satellite internet, Amazon splashed out billions of dollars to reserve debuts on 38 Vulcan Centaur rockets, 18 Arianespace Ariane 6es, and anywhere from 12 to 27 Blue Origin Upcoming Glenns.

    Industry observers note that it's also reserved debuts on some of ULA's older Atlas V rockets. So far, those have done most of the work of putting nearly 400 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit (with significant help from SpaceX's Falcon 9, which Amazon reluctantly added to the lineup in 2023). The problem is, ULA is just about out of Atlas V rockets (and isn't building more). And SpaceX Falcon 9 launches are all booked up through 2028 (and SpaceX also doesn't plan to add more).

    Industry observers note that this leaves Amazon largely dependent on ULA's Vulcan Centaur -- which just proved itself unreliable. And this problem may get even bigger; after all, the same BE-4 engine that appears to be at the root of Vulcan's problems also powers Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. And that could put New Glenn on the sidelines as well.

    (Or it may not. While the investigation is still at an early stage, as of Wednesday, ULA believes "preliminary indications" suggest Vulcan's fuel supply to the BE-4 engines, and not the engines themselves, is the culprit. If that's the case, then Blue Origin's New Glenn may not be affected.).

    Still, until this is all resolved, it appears that Amazon right now has no reliable means of putting Leo satellites into orbit.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, in the meantime, SpaceX Starlink, already the leader in satellite internet, is likely to remain so for the foreseeable future. More than that: the longer Amazon is forced to cool its heels down here on Earth, the wider the gap between SpaceX and [insert name of literally anyone else who might want to compete with SpaceX].

    Amazon's pain, I fear, is going to be SpaceX's gain.

    According to recent reports, management executed a reduction in force (RIF: a planned, permanent elimination of job positions) to lower operating expenses following operational integration delays and legacy overhead. Lowering headcount aligns cost structures with current shipment volumes while the company works to eliminate non-cash accounts receivable (AR: unpaid customer invoices) write-offs.

    Long-term power market trends continue to favor solar adoption as utility electricity costs increase, and management is not hiding its focus on expanding high-margin sales channels.

    The manufacturer relies on pre-assembled roof installation kits and exclusive supply agreements for high-efficiency solar modules to protect project margins. Management is watching conversion rates on its work-in-process (WIP: active jobs moving through assembly), state-level expansion, and positive operating cash flow within two quarters.

    Growth now hinges on scaling commercial contracts and expanding virtual power plant deployments across latest geographic markets to surpass baseline residential revenue.

    Billionaire David Tepper Just Made a Massive AI Chip Rotation — Will It Pay Off?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.
    • David Tepper of Appaloosa Management is considered one of the world's top hedge fund managers, and through his investment prowess, he's amassed an estimated net worth of $28.5 billion.
    • In a recent development, while Tepper's track record speaks for itself, I think he got it wrong in this case.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 21, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

    David Tepper of Appaloosa Management is considered one of the world's top hedge fund managers, and through his investment prowess, he's amassed an estimated net worth of $28.5 billion. The Carolina Panthers' owner was reshuffling his artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor positions in Q3, exiting positions in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) and Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%), while buying shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) and Micron (MU -13.89%). He also cut his stake in Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) nearly in half.

    In a recent development, while Tepper's track record speaks for itself, I think he got it wrong in this case. Here's why.

    It has been revealed that while Tepper was buying Nvidia shares before Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO, the company is facing potential challenges beyond the loss of its CEO. Competitors have started to catch up, with Semianalysis recently reporting that Alphabet's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which it co-developed with Broadcom, are delivering better performance per dollar. Meanwhile, all of Nvidia's largest customers, outside of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) are working on developing their own custom chips.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that the AI application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) market is growing much more quickly than the GPU market, with Counterpoint Research projecting that custom AI chip unit shipments will surpass data center GPU shipments in 2028. Two of the biggest winners from this trend are Alphabet and Broadcom.

    Alphabet developed its TPUs more than a decade ago, and its comprehensive ecosystem is starting to rival Nvidia's. Not only is TPU growth supported by Alphabet's internal use and its cloud offering, but it is also beginning to sell its solutions to external data center operators, such as Anthropic and OpenAI.

    It has been revealed that bloomberg Intelligence believes that TPU sales outside of Google Cloud could grow from just $12 billion this year to over $135 billion in 2028. This is a huge revenue driver for both Alphabet and Broadcom, which appear to be two of the biggest winners in this rotation.

    Even bigger news for Nvidia competitors, though, is that Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) revealed that its Claude Mythos model demonstrated that it can get models up to speed running on AMD GPUs in just two to three days without any human involvement, dramatically cutting down the six to 12 months it used to take a dozen engineers to get models running on different chips. This greatly narrows Nvidia's CUDA moat and opens the door for both AMD and ASICs to take market share.

    The timing is great for AMD, as it recently started shipping its complete Helios systems, which combine its GPUs, CPUs, and networking into one package, to large hyperscaler customers. It's significantly cheaper than Nvidia's end-to-end server racks, opening the door to take more market share if it can show strong performance. The company's CPUs will also play a key role in Alphabet's new TPU 8tx AI system.

    It has been revealed that with CUDA's moat weakening, Alphabet, Broadcom, and AMD, all of which have cheaper offerings, should benefit greatly in the coming years. Meanwhile, Nvidia could face not just a loss of share but also margin compression. This could lead to lower profitability even if it can grow its revenue. That's one of the major reasons I prefer the three stocks Tepper was selling over Nvidia.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that as for the other semiconductor stock that Tepper was buying, Micron, I'd be careful. Memory has historically experienced very big boom-and-bust cycles, and, while this supercycle is certainly different, memory still tends to be a commodity.

    Micron is also the most exposed of the massive dynamic random access memory (DRAM) makers to any changes in prices of conventional memory, with it having the smallest share of the high bandwidth memory (HBM) market, which has been the driving force of the industry.

    Another area of worry is with NAND, or flash memory. While Micron derives the bulk of its memory from DRAM, NAND has grown to about a quarter of its revenue. Hong Kong-based GF Securities recently issued a note saying it expects this market to become oversupplied as soon as next year. While primarily a DRAM maker, Micron would not be immune to a big price pullback in the NAND market.
